subject: Post-call: performance SLOs & customer-led load test (FinWise)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Patel <evan.patel@finwise.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance SLOs & customer-led load test (FinWise)

Thanks for the call today — great to align. Quick recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of SLO / workload requirements (as discussed)
- Target p95 latency: <= 300ms (inference end-to-end, 512 tokens average)
- Throughput: sustained 150 req/s (burst to 400 req/s for brief windows)
- Target concurrency: 40-60 concurrent sessions (typical 50)
- Streaming: required for partial responses (client expects chunked tokens)
- Auth: API key for test account; we'll provide a dedicated test key and scoped dataset
- Error budget tolerance: up to 1% errors during load test window

Customer-led load test details requested
- Tools: FinWise prefers k6 but can run Locust if needed (they'll send scripts)
- Test account: want a non-prod API key + test model variant (we can spin up a dedicated pool)
- IP allowlist: FinWise needs our public egress IP ranges to allowlist on their side and will provide their test IPs for our allowlist.
- Test windows: propose Thu 2027-03-25 09:00-12:00 PT (primary) and Fri 2027-03-26 02:00-05:00 PT (backup)

Action items
- Marissa: provision test API key + scoped test account, send allowlist ranges and sample headers (by EOD Tue)
- Logan: confirm whether we can provision a temporary dedicated pool sized for 150 req/s with burst headroom and streaming enabled; note any rate limits.
- Rishi: review customer's k6 script once they send and flag any API call patterns that could cause KV cache misses or cold-starts.
- FinWise (Evan/Sana): share k6 script and source IP list; confirm which geo to run from (us-west/oregon preferred).

Attachments: slo-summary.pdf (SLO recap), sample k6 test harness (placeholder)

Thanks — I’ll send the test account details once Logan confirms capacity.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Evan Patel <evan.patel@finwise.com>

Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance SLOs & customer-led load test (FinWise)

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right to us. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We'll run the primary test from our US West (Oregon) cloud nodes.
- k6 is our primary harness; attaching the initial k6 script we'll run for the 150 req/s baseline. (Attachment: k6-loadscript-v1.js)
- Test IPs from our side (source) that you should allowlist to accept inbound callbacks: 18.205.93.0/24, 3.234.210.0/24
- We will not run the burst phase until we confirm staging passes; primary baseline run Thu 09:00-10:30 PT and then ramp test 10:30-11:30 PT.

Can you please provide:
1) Test API key + endpoint details
2) Your public egress IP ranges so our network/security team can allowlist callbacks
3) Any headers or throttling behavior to include in the k6 script (e.g., X-Redwood-Client, quota headers)

Evan

Thanks — provided below and attached a small README. 

1) Test API key and endpoint (scoped to FinWise test env)
- Endpoint: https://api-test.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- API Key: rw_test_finwise_20270322_xxx (note: key is scoped to test project, expires 2027-04-30)

2) Our current public egress IP ranges (for callbacks and webhooks)
- 13.57.0.0/18
- 52.10.0.0/16
(we'll give a longer-term list in the provisioning ticket; these two ranges are sufficient for the short window)

3) Headers / throttling notes for k6 script
- Required headers: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>, X-Redwood-Client: finwise-loadtest
- Recommended concurrency pattern: steady-state 150 req/s with 5m warmup, then 1m ramp to 400 req/s for 10m
- Response codes: treat 429 as retryable, 5xx as failures to report. We will log and surface 5xx counts to you immediately.

Attachments included: redwood-test-account.txt (contains API key and endpoint), sample k6 snippet, slo-summary.pdf

Logan / Rishi: can you confirm the dedicated pool sizing and whether we need to disable any IP-based rate limits on the test key? Ideally we grant elevated burst for a 90-minute window.

--
Marissa

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance SLOs & customer-led load test (FinWise)

Spun up a temporary dedicated pool for FinWise test (tags: finwise-loadtest-20270325):
- Provisioned capacity: supports sustained 200 req/s at p95 ~260ms for 512-token avg.
- Burst headroom: up to 500 req/s for short windows (we'll monitor heat/queueing).
- Streaming: enabled on that pool.
- Rate limits: test API key has relaxed rate limit for 90-minute window (2027-03-25T16:00:00Z to 2027-03-25T17:30:00Z) to match the proposed 09:00-10:30 PT window.

Notes and follow-ups:
- We enabled higher concurrent KV cache size to avoid cold-cache on ramp, but expect some KV cache misses at the start of the baseline. Rishi: please watch for >5% cache miss during ramp and advise if we should pre-warm.
- Security: IP ranges Marissa provided look good for callbacks; internal policy requires a ticket for permanent allowlist.
- I reviewed the customer's k6 script — converting a couple of POSTs to use chunked transfer looks fine. Sent inline comments to Rishi separately.

I'll be available in the test channel during the window. If FinWise wants a quick sync before Thu morning to sanity-check the script, I can join.

-Logan
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
